prompts.prompt: Create one NEW compact educational whiteboard diagram for a Korean introductory optimization notebook. The attached slide is only a reference for the hand-drawn whiteboard style, not content to copy. Rebuild as a standalone clean white background illustration; no slide frame, no title, no logo, no watermark, no source citation. Simple black marker axes with subtle natural hand-drawn strokes, blue smooth upward-opening parabola f(x)=½x². Accurate mathematical plot: vertex at (0,0), current point at (2,2) on the RIGHT branch in orange. Green dot at vertex. Axis horizontal x and vertical f(x). Plot shows x from about -1.5 to 2.5. The ONLY labels, handwritten clean mathematical italic lettering: 'f(x) = ½x²' near upper left; 'x = 2' below horizontal coordinate 2; 'x_next = 0' below origin using next as a real subscript, NOT literal underscore; 'f(2) = 2' near current orange point; 'f(0) = 0' near green vertex. Place a dashed orange vertical projection from (2,2) to horizontal axis. Below axis, a horizontal orange arrow points LEFT from coordinate 2 to coordinate 0, labeled 'Δx = −2'. No curved arrow implying movement along graph. No tangent line. No decorative objects, no people, no handwriting tools. One focused panel, landscape ~3:2. All lettering same modest size, designed to appear like 16px adjacent body text when whole image displayed 480 CSS pixels wide; avoid oversized letters. Fill canvas compactly with modest margins. Use legible consistent mathematical notation: x_next is x with next subscript. This diagram shows the objective reduction after a Newton update; it is not a root-finding diagram.

Create one NEW compact educational whiteboard diagram for a Korean introductory optimization notebook. Attached slide is only a reference for hand-drawn whiteboard style; create a clean standalone diagram from scratch with no copied content. Pure white background, lightly hand-drawn black axes, blue straight line f′(x)=x increasing from bottom left through origin to upper right. This is a graph of the DERIVATIVE, not the objective. Horizontal axis x, vertical axis f′(x). Orange point at (2,2), teal green point at (0,0). Mark the rise/run triangle with light blue dotted segments from (0,0) horizontally to (2,0), then vertically to (2,2). Label horizontal segment with small '2' and vertical with small '2' so curvature is visually rise/run = 1. Put small formula 'f″(x) = 2/2 = 1' at upper LEFT, not overlapping line. Put 'f′(x) = x' by blue line near top RIGHT. Label orange point 'f′(2) = 2' offset to its upper left. Below axis, label horizontal coordinate 2 as 'x = 2', origin as 'x_next = 0' using proper subscript next. Draw orange horizontal LEFT arrow from coordinate 2 to coordinate 0 below axis, labeled 'Δx = −2'. No parabola, no extraneous formulas, no title, no borders, no watermark, no source, no decorative marker objects. One focused landscape panel ~3:2, moderate margins. All lettering should be clean handwritten mathematical italic style and similarly sized, appearing about 16px at 480 CSS pixels display width. Subscripts and derivative prime marks must be exact. Match ordinary whiteboard teaching notes, restrained palette blue for graph, orange current point/update, teal green target, black formulas.

Generate a new compact educational whiteboard illustration, matching the provided reference's hand-written marker style, white background, blue decisions, orange movement arrows, purple learning-rate labels. No title, no frame, no decorative objects. One focused landscape panel, intended to display at only 480 CSS px wide. All lettering should read like 16px body text at that size, with generous separation. Content: comparison of TWO learning rates at the SAME starting x=2 and SAME gradient f′(2)=2. Draw two parallel horizontal number lines, both with coordinate ticks at x=0, x=1, x=1.5 and x=2, exactly aligned across rows. Current point x=2 at far right is orange in both rows. Upper row: purple label α=0.25 on left above line; arrow points LEFT from x=2 to x=1.5; small blue destination dot at x=1.5; annotate orange arrow 'Δx = −0.5'. Lower row: purple label α=0.5 on left above line; arrow points LEFT from x=2 to x=1; small blue destination dot at x=1; annotate orange arrow 'Δx = −1'. ONE common small black formula 'f′(2) = 2' above both rows. Coordinate labels below each row 0,1,1.5,2 in small consistent handwriting, horizontal axis x at right. Keep labels and arrows apart. This is gradient descent: changing only learning rate changes movement length. No parabola. No new functions. No additional explanatory text. Exact mathematics with properly printed Greek alpha and delta, genuine prime symbol.

Generate a new compact hand-written whiteboard educational diagram matching the supplied reference style. White background, restrained marker strokes, no frame, no title, no watermark, no decoration. It explains Newton's update Δx = −g/c for a fixed local gradient g=2 while only curvature c changes. At top put ONE modest formula 'g = 2' (g refers to current f′(x)). Two rows below with horizontal displacement number lines, perfectly aligned and equally scaled: tick values −2 at left, −1 in middle, 0 at right. Small black axis label Δx at far right of each line. Both rows start at displacement 0 with orange point. Upper row label in blue 'c = 1', arrow LEFT from displacement 0 to displacement −2, label '−2/1 = −2' above arrow, destination dot blue. Lower row label blue 'c = 2', arrow LEFT from displacement 0 to displacement −1, label '−2/2 = −1' above arrow, destination dot blue. Orange arrows, black numerical arithmetic labels. Keep formulas separated from axes. Only show the specified labels; prose will be in surrounding notebook. The fixed gradient is NOT a new objective: these are two local curvature assumptions. No parabola, no slope graph, no current x coordinate labels, axes are displacement Δx ONLY. Aspect ratio landscape around 3:2; all text similarly sized, appears approximately 16px at final display width 460 CSS px. Clean mathematical italic lettering, no big headings.

Create a compact educational whiteboard diagram matching reference's neat handwritten marker style, white background, no title, no frame, no decorative objects. A simple THREE-STEP VERTICAL calculation strip, intended to be displayed only 400 CSS px wide, overall roughly square. All text handwritten mathematical style with similar modest lettering size, no oversized headline. First row label Korean '갱신 후' and formula 'x_next ≈ 7.7 × 10⁻⁸' where next is a proper subscript of x. Thin blue downward arrow. Second row label Korean '기울기 검사' and exact formula '|f′(x_next)| ≈ 7.7 × 10⁻⁸' (this example f′(x)=x). Thin blue downward arrow. Third row a light teal hand-drawn outline box with formula '7.7 × 10⁻⁸ < ε = 10⁻⁶' and small green checkmark, with Korean label '종료 기준 충족'. Represent exponents carefully, all 10 powers as proper superscripts, f derivative with prime, next as subscript. This explains checking the UPDATED gradient, not step length or objective value. Do not claim general minimum guaranteed. No objective curve, no branch logic, no additional words. Dark black formulas, teal green final check, blue connectors. Balanced blank margins; modest letters should appear around 16px at 400 CSS px display width.

Edit this hand-drawn teaching diagram only to use the SAME notation as the surrounding Newton lesson. Replace the top 'g = 2' with 'f′(x) = 2'. Replace upper blue 'c = 1' with 'f″(x) = 1', and lower blue 'c = 2' with 'f″(x) = 2'. Keep all other arithmetic, positions, arrows, colors, both displacement axes Δx and their tick values −2, −1, 0 unchanged. No new labels or decorations. Slightly reduce the lettering of all three replacement labels to match the arithmetic labels, avoiding large heading-like text. Mathematical prime and double-prime symbols must be clear; f″ is the second derivative. Preserve whiteboard marker style and white background.
